title: Fix crash on closed generic structs from referenced assemblies

lines.text: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).

Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
Members of a type defined in a referenced assembly are reported by the project that defines that type, so an unattributed public member of such a type must be fixed in its defining project.

requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement.intent: A [MessagePackObject] type with a member whose type is a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly must build cleanly and still get a generated resolver.

functional.text: The generator does not throw when a member's type is a closed generic struct or record struct defined in a referenced assembly.
The analyzer does not throw for the same member types.
The compiling assembly gets its generated resolver, as it does when the generic type is declared in the same project.

nonFunctional.text: A failure of the generator or analyzer must not pass silently as a build warning that leaves the assembly without a resolver. (inferred)
Behaviour for generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same project does not change. (inferred)

expectedBehaviours: Compiling a project whose [MessagePackObject] type has a member typed as a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly (for example ExternalStruct<int>) produces no IndexOutOfRangeException from the source generator.
The same holds when the referenced type is a closed generic record struct.
No generator warning such as CS8785 (generator failed and will not contribute output) shows up for these member types.
expectedTests: A generator snapshot test with a referenced compilation that defines a generic struct, and a consuming [MessagePackObject] type with a closed instance of it as a member, runs with no generator exceptions and no failure diagnostics.
A variant of that test uses a generic record struct from the referenced assembly and also finishes without exceptions.

expectedBehaviours: Running the MessagePack analyzers on a [MessagePackObject] type with a member of a closed generic struct or record struct from a referenced assembly throws no IndexOutOfRangeException.
No AD0001 (analyzer threw an exception) diagnostic appears for these member types.
The analyzer still reports any real MsgPack diagnostics that apply, and adds no false ones because of the external generic type.
expectedTests: An analyzer test whose additional metadata reference defines a generic struct checks that no AD0001 or unexpected MsgPack diagnostics are reported for a member that uses a closed instance of it.
The same analyzer test with a generic record struct reports no exceptions.

expectedBehaviours: The consuming assembly gets the generated resolver, and its formatter for the [MessagePackObject] type covers the member of the external closed generic struct type.
The generated output has the same shape as when the generic struct is declared in the same project.
At runtime the type round-trips through serialization using the generated resolver.
expectedTests: A snapshot test compares the generated resolver and formatter sources for the cross-assembly closed generic struct case against expected files under Resources.
A runtime test serializes and deserializes an object with such a member through the generated resolver and gets back an equal value.

expectedBehaviours: When the generator hits an unexpected condition with such types, the build does not end up with only a warning and an assembly that has no resolver.
Generator and analyzer failures for these inputs show up visibly, either as a clear error diagnostic or as a failing test, rather than a silently missing resolver.
expectedTests: Generator tests fail when the generator reports an exception diagnostic or produces no resolver for the cross-assembly generic struct input, instead of only logging a warning.

expectedBehaviours: Generated output for generic classes, non-generic structs and generic types declared in the same project matches the existing snapshots.

story.what: The change stops TypeCollector from indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] when it builds the MemberNeedsKey (field) and BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull (property) diagnostics. A member that comes from metadata has no syntax references, so this indexing threw. It also wraps the analyzer's report callback so that a diagnostic is dropped unless its location is a source tree in the compilation being analyzed. Three new generator tests compile the defining code to a metadata-only image and check two things: that the analyzers and the generator report no diagnostics, and that the resolver source is generated. README and the MsgPack004 doc now say that diagnostics for types from referenced assemblies are reported by the project that defines them.
story.why: Issue 2283 (MP-2283): a [MessagePackObject] member typed as a closed generic struct or record struct from a referenced assembly made the generator and the analyzer throw IndexOutOfRangeException. The generator failure showed up only as a warning, and the assembly was left without a resolver.

touches.note: reportDiagnostic is now a wrapper that sends each diagnostic through ReportIfLocatedInCompilation.
The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull and field MemberNeedsKey locations no longer index DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].
New helper. Returns the property identifier location, or null when the property has no PropertyDeclarationSyntax.
New filter. Reports a diagnostic only when its location is in source and in a syntax tree of the compilation.
New helper. Emits the defining source to an image, runs the verifier, then runs the generator driver and asserts that the resolver hint name is present.

claims.text: For an unkeyed field, the MemberNeedsKey diagnostic now takes its location from DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()? instead of DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]. This diagnostic is assigned to a local without any check on reportDiagnostic, so the old indexing ran in generator mode too, where reportDiagnostic is null. A field of a metadata type has no syntax references, so the old code threw IndexOutOfRangeException. Compiler-generated backing fields of a metadata record struct are one possible source of such fields.

evidence.summary: Quote checked against the code at src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1077–1077

claims.text: The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic for a property now gets its location from the new GetPropertyIdentifierLocation helper. The helper uses FirstOrDefault and an 'as PropertyDeclarationSyntax' cast, and returns null for metadata properties. The old code did a hard cast on DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0], which threw for metadata properties. For properties declared in source, the helper returns the same identifier location as before.

evidence.summary: Quote checked against the code at src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:985–985

claims.text: When an analyzer callback is supplied, the constructor now wraps it in ReportIfLocatedInCompilation. The wrapper forwards a diagnostic only if diagnostic.Location.IsInSource is true and the compilation contains the location's syntax tree. As a result, diagnostics about members of types from referenced assemblies are dropped silently instead of being reported. The InaccessibleDataType report in the constructor still uses the raw reportAnalyzerDiagnostic and does not go through this filter.

citations.quote: this.reportDiagnostic = reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is null ? null : diagnostic => ReportIfLocatedInCompilation(reportAnalyzerDiagnostic, diagnostic);

evidence.summary: Quote checked against the code at src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:239–239

claims.text: The filter is broader than metadata types. Any diagnostic created with a null location gets Location.None, so IsInSource is false and the diagnostic is now dropped even when the type is declared in the project being compiled. Several diagnostics can be built with a null location for source types, for example MemberNeedsKey when no property or parameter identifier is found, and PartialTypeRequired when primaryLocation is null. Before this change they were reported without a location, and now they are suppressed. No test covers this.
